title: zeroTT: A Two-Step State Transition Avoidance Scheme for MLC STT-RAM
problem: MLC STT-RAM suffers from degraded write performance due to two-step state transitions (TTs) occurring in memory cells' soft domain. Existing coding approaches only reduce TTs but cannot fully eliminate them.
motivation: STT-RAM offers superior storage density and power efficiency compared to SRAM for embedded systems, with MLC variants providing even better bit density than SLC.
method: zeroTT employs an optimal (3,4)-based expansion coding scheme that completely eliminates two-step state transitions in MLC STT-RAM. The design balances space overhead and coding complexity to achieve full state transition elimination while maintaining practical feasibility.
key_novelty: First coding scheme to completely eliminate state transitions in MLC STT-RAM rather than merely reducing them.
contributions: Optimal (3,4)-based expansion coding method that completely avoids state transitions
Design accounting for both space overhead and coding complexity tradeoffs
Demonstration of improvements in access latency, energy consumption, and device lifetime
primary_theme: Memory coding for STT-RAM performance optimization
